ambiguities.description: Exam room number is mentioned as an identifier ('Exam rooms have a room number'), but no fact type or relationship associates exam rooms with appointments, patients, or doctors anywhere in the transcript. ambiguities.description: The appointment scheduling constraints mention that patients and doctors have time-slot-based scheduling ('we book in fixed slots'). It's unclear whether a patient can have at most one appointment per date/time slot, and whether a doctor can have at most one appointment per date/time slot -- these scheduling exclusivity rules are common in clinic domains but not explicitly stated here.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: Is the appointment status list closed permanently (fixed enumeration) or could new statuses be added later? Also is status a stored attribute or could it be derived from other events (e.g., check-in event, completion event)? Not clarified.

source_references.excerpt: The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

ambiguities.description: Doctor specialty is described as singular ('Every doctor has exactly one specialty'), but no value constraint list is given as with appointment status. Is Specialty a fixed enumerated value type, or free text? The examples given (cardiology, general practice) suggest a domain of values but it isn't stated to be exhaustive.

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

ambiguities.description: The relationship 'patient has primary doctor' is distinct from 'appointment is with doctor' per the stakeholder, but it's unclear if there are any constraints linking the two (e.g., must the primary doctor ever be the one seen in an appointment, or are they fully independent facts with no cross constraint)?

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.

ambiguities.description: Temporal tracking: Is the assignment of 'primary doctor' to a patient historical (can change over time, requiring history) or just current-state? The transcript doesn't mention change-over-time semantics for primary doctor, doctor specialty, or appointment status transitions.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor.

ambiguities.description: Granularity: 'Visit reason' and 'follow-up note' are treated as free-text value types, but it's unclear if these need more structure (e.g., categorized reasons) or if plain text is sufficient given no further detail was given.
